title: Probe ensemble with rate-budgeted load shedding for SLO consistency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During multi-region incidents we observe sharp autoscaler oscillations and cascading degradation where aggressive readiness gating causes large capacity drops that then push traffic to fallback regions, creating cross-region hotspots and SLO violations. Existing readiness/liveness probes are single-signal and use tight windows which amplify noisy failures.

Goal: Implement a probe ensemble and a rate-budgeted, tiered load-shedding mechanism that preserves P99 latency and availability SLOs during transient regional degradations while enabling controlled failover to other regions. The approach should reduce autoscaler thrash and provide deterministic circuit-breaker behavior for high-priority customer routes.
acceptance_criteria: Probe ensemble implemented in runtime and configurable per route/region
Rate budgets per route enforced with measurable shedding behavior under overload
Autoscaler oscillation metric (scale events per minute) reduced by >=40% in sim runs
End-to-end demo: simulated regional outage does not increase cross-region P99 by more than 10% for gold routes
Feature gated behind runtime flag and opt-in config for Dedicated/Private customers
technical_notes: Design: combine three signals into a single readiness score: (1) local health probe success rate over an adaptive window, (2) synthetic transaction latency/success, (3) runtime backpressure metric (active inflight + queue depth). Each signal normalized and weighted by route importance.
Windowing: use exponentially-weighted windows with separate decay constants for short (10s) and medium (120s) horizons to avoid reacting to microbursts while still detecting sustained degradation.

Budgeting: allocate a per-route token budget (requests/sec) used only during degraded mode. Budgets are region-local and backed by a central policy that can shift tokens to adjacent regions during controlled failover.

Shedding policy: implement tiered shedding by priority: 1) low-cost cheap early-reject for background/low-priority routes, 2) queued delay for medium-priority, 3) graceful reject with structured error + retry hint for high-priority but non-critical requests. Gold routes have circuit-breaker thresholds that prefer routing to fallback region before shedding.

Autoscaler integration: add hysteresis to scale-down decisions tied to ensemble readiness score and 'minimum-serving-weight' per region to prevent immediate scale-down after probe failures. Scale-up remains responsive but subject to a short cooldown to reduce thrash.
Observability: expose ensemble score, budget consumption, shed counts, and circuit-breaker state to Console and Grafana dashboards; add tracing tags to identify shed decisions in request traces.
decisions: Do runtime gating (server-side) instead of changing client SDK timeouts — keeps client surface unchanged and centralizes safe defaults.
Keep per-route budgets small by default and enable explicit opt-in for routes requiring aggressive cross-region failover to avoid accidental cost increases.
Implement feature flag 'probe_ensemble_v1' scoped by org so we can roll out in Dedicated first and monitor before enabling hosted customers.
design_feedback: PM review (Tomas Rivera): suggested clearer backward compatibility notes and migration path for existing readiness configs — added in design doc.
SRE review (Priya Nair): asked for chaos test plan to validate late-arriving KV cache invalidation interactions — added to test plan.
Security review (Jamal Okoye): confirmed no additional customer data exported; recommended encrypting token budget control-plane traffic — backlog item created.
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike completed — simulated ensemble in emulator; early results show 38% reduction in scale-down events under noisy probe patterns.
2026-03-09: Initial implementation of ensemble scoring merged behind feature flag (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287).
2026-03-11: Integration test added for per-route budget accounting; found race where token recharge could overshoot after region failover — patch prepared.
risks_and_mitigation: False positives: the ensemble can incorrectly mark healthy nodes as unhealthy if weights are mis-tuned. Mitigation: use conservative default weights and a short canary rollout while capturing false-positive telemetry.
Cost risk: enabling cross-region token shifting may increase egress costs. Mitigation: budgets are opt-in for each org/route and default to local-only behavior.
Complexity for ops: new metrics/circuit states increase operational surface. Mitigation: provide a Console playbook and an automated runbook to revert to simple readiness gating.
test_plan: Unit tests for ensemble normalization, weight updates, and window decay semantics.
Load tests in staging with noisy probe injection and synthetic failover to measure P99 and scale events per minute.
Chaos experiment: delayed backend KV lookups + regional network partition to validate shedding and token migration behavior.
Canary rollout on two Dedicated customers with ops runbook and pair-of-engineers rotation.
next_steps: Finish patch for token recharge race and land PR (target: 2026-03-15).
Add Grafana panels and Console widgets for ensemble score and budget heatmap (assigned to observability team).
Run full staging load test with synthetic region outage (target: 2026-03-22).
Schedule canary with two Dedicated customers and collect SLO metrics for 72h before broader rollout.
